findings.source: engine/reconstruction/src/TextureBaker.cpp: rasterizeDepth() called for every prepared camera over source.vertices/source.indices
findings.consequence: A bake rebuilds each camera depth oracle from the full mesh; local geometry changes are not currently represented as screen-space dirty depth regions.

findings.source: TextureBaker.cpp loops every triangle and every prepared camera before truncating to maximumCamerasPerTriangle
findings.consequence: Candidate selection is globally O(triangles*cameras) even for a local mesh change.

findings.source: targetLogLuminance = median(cameraMedians); every camera exposure gain is derived from this target
findings.consequence: A source-image/exposure change can alter a camera gain, and in threshold cases the global median target, invalidating texels beyond the changed spatial region.

findings.source: columns=ceil(sqrt(triangleCount)); rows/cell derive from total triangleCount; tileX/tileY derive from triangle ordinal
findings.consequence: Triangle insertion/removal/reordering can change UV addresses of unchanged triangles; threshold crossings can globally change atlas cell dimensions.

findings.source: gutter iterations scan almost the entire atlas
findings.consequence: Even if only a few triangle tiles change, final dilation currently performs global atlas work.

decision: Do not claim texture-level locality from spatial dirty regions. Exact incremental texture repair requires stable triangle/patch identity, stable atlas addressing, localized visibility/depth dependencies, and a photometric policy whose dependency scope is explicit.
nextProbes: atlas-uv-churn-v0: quantify unchanged-triangle UV churn under local triangle insertion/removal in current ordinal layout
stable-patch-atlas-v0: compare fixed page/patch allocation overhead vs UV stability
exposure-coupling-v0: perturb one camera's exposure samples and measure number of camera gains/texels theoretically invalidated
screen-space-depth-dependency-v0: map changed mesh patch bounds to affected cameras and depth tiles
